title: Microsoft Purview: permanently delete OneDrive and SharePoint files with Priority cleanup
summary: The briefing's deletion behaviour, approval safeguards, rollout dates and operational controls are supported by Microsoft's documentation and notice. Minor corrections concern references for two PowerShell parameter mentions and checklist instructions without corresponding control rows.

claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Purview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on 26 October 2026 at 23:15:50.
Priority Cleanup has an additional permanent deletion option for targeted SharePoint and OneDrive files.
claims.quote: Use Microsoft Purview Priority Cleanup to permanently delete targeted files from SharePoint and OneDrive after the required review and approval.

claims.claim: Permanent deletion bypasses the SharePoint and OneDrive recycle bins, removing that recovery route.

claims.claim: A query defines the targeted files.
claims.quote: Enter the policy name and description, choose an adaptive or static scope, select the SharePoint or OneDrive locations, and define the query for the targeted files.

claims.claim: The policy can delete matched items as soon as possible or prevent deletion until a set time.
claims.quote: Choose whether to delete matched items as soon as possible or prevent deletion until a set time.

claims.quote: Assign the required approvers.

claims.quote: After the simulation results are satisfactory, have a second Priority Cleanup admin review the results and turn on the policy.

claims.claim: The last person to edit a policy cannot also turn it on.
claims.quote: The last person to edit the policy can't also turn it on.

claims.claim: Approvers use Approve disposal under Pending cleanups to approve permanent deletion.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, go to Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > Pending cleanups. Select the cleanup and review the identified items, their locations, and their history. Select the items to delete, and then select Approve disposal.

claims.quote: Items already copied to an eDiscovery review set aren't deleted by Priority Cleanup.

claims.claim: MC1261587 was updated on 26 October 2026.
claims.quote: Updated October 26, 2026: We have updated the timeline.

claims.claim: The notice targets public preview rollout beginning mid-August 2026.
claims.quote: Public Preview: We will begin rolling out mid-August 2026 (previously mid-July)

claims.claim: The notice targets completion of public preview rollout by end of November 2026.
claims.quote: expect to complete by end of November 2026 (previously mid-September).

claims.claim: The notice targets Worldwide General Availability rollout beginning end of November 2026.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide) Rollout begins end of November 2026 (previously mid-October)

claims.claim: The notice targets completion of General Availability rollout by early January 2027.
claims.quote: is expected to complete by early January 2027 (previously end of November 2026).

claims.claim: The permanent deletion Learn page says public preview rollout begins on August 24, 2026.
claims.quote: Confirm that the permanent deletion option is available in your tenant. Public preview rollout begins on August 24, 2026.

claims.claim: The supplied notice sets no act-by date and requires no mandatory enablement action.
claims.quote: Act by: none; This capability is not enabled by default and requires explicit admin configuration.

claims.claim: The roadmap description says retention policies and labels keep deleted SharePoint and OneDrive content in recycle bins for 93 days.
claims.quote: M365 retention labels policies and M365 retention policies do not hard delete content immediately and keeps the data in Recycle Bins for 93 days for ODSP.

claims.claim: The roadmap identifies data spillage as a use case.
claims.quote: Priority Cleanup feature allows users to bypass retention, and eDiscovery holds to help customers comply to changing legal/compliance requirements or manage data spillage scenarios.

claims.claim: Microsoft positions the change as reducing exposure from growing Copilot-related content, including Teams transcripts.
claims.quote: This capability helps reduce data exposure risk from rapidly growing Copilot-related content; Review your organization’s data risk and retention strategy, especially for Copilot-generated content such as Teams transcripts.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The permanent deletion capability is admin-opt-in rather than enabled by default.
claims.quote: This capability is not enabled by default and requires explicit admin configuration.

claims.claim: User workflows do not change unless an admin configures and applies a Priority Cleanup policy.
claims.quote: There is no change to user workflows unless an admin configures and applies a priority cleanup policy.

claims.claim: The surrounding tenant-level Priority Cleanup feature is enabled by default.
claims.quote: Because of the built-in safeguards, the feature itself is enabled by default at the tenant level.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive Priority Cleanup requires simulation at least once.
claims.quote: For SharePoint and OneDrive, you must run simulation at least one time, and for any change other than the policy description.

claims.claim: Learn's overview says Priority Cleanup can override Preservation Lock for delete-only retention settings.
claims.quote: Because the deletion from priority cleanup can override existing holds and even Preservation Lock when the retention settings are for delete-only

claims.claim: The same Learn page's Limitations section says delete-only Preservation Lock items are not in scope outside simulation.
claims.quote: In simulation mode, items under preservation lock where the retention settings are configured for delete-only may show up. These items are not actually in scope for priority cleanup outside simulation mode.

claims.claim: Learn describes multiple approvals, specific roles and auditing as Priority Cleanup safeguards.
claims.quote: the process requires multiple approvals, specific roles, and is audited.

claims.claim: Priority Cleanup Admin is required to create and manage these policies.
claims.quote: Assign the Priority Cleanup Admin role to the administrator who creates and manages the policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Priority Cleanup Admin is automatically added to Organization Management, giving that group's members access.
claims.quote: To successfully access and manage Priority cleanup in the Microsoft Purview portal, you must have the Priority Cleanup Admin role. This role is automatically added to the Organization Management role group but must be manually added to any other role group.

claims.claim: Each cleanup item requires approval by at least one person other than the policy creator.
claims.quote: each item subject to priority cleanup always requires at least one other person to approve the deletion in addition to the person who created the priority cleanup policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Items under eDiscovery holds additionally require eDiscovery admin approval.
claims.quote: If an item is also subject to one or more eDiscovery holds, eDiscovery admin approval is also required.

claims.claim: Learn recommends leaving a cleanup policy running for continually created Teams recordings and transcripts.
claims.quote: Because these files are continually created, leave the priority cleanup policy running to automatically find and delete the stale files.

claims.claim: Policy creation fails with an error if an eDiscovery reviewer lacks the correct roles in advance.
claims.quote: If the reviewer for eDiscovery admin doesn't have the correct roles assigned in advance, policy creation fails with an error.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: A separate price or licensing rule specific to the permanent deletion option is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Priority cleanup" "permanent deletion" license pricing meter. Read permanent-deletion prerequisites, the Purview service description's Priority cleanup licensing list, and purview-billing-models; no distinct permanent-deletion price or licence rule.

claims.claim: The permanent deletion page's prerequisites name roles, approvers, auditing and simulation but no licence.
claims.quote: Before you begin, review the required roles, approvers, auditing, and simulation requirements.

claims.claim: No meter or per-deletion charge is documented for this feature as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Priority cleanup" "permanent deletion" license pricing meter. Read priority-cleanup-permanent-deletion, the Purview service description and purview-billing-models, including its DLM meter for non-Microsoft 365 AI interactions; none documents a file-cleanup meter.

claims.claim: Learn does not document a separate tenant switch for the permanent deletion option itself.
claims.quote: Searched: "priority cleanup" "permanent deletion" "switch". Read priority-cleanup-permanent-deletion and priority-cleanup-onedrive-sharepoint, including Turn off priority cleanup for the tenant; only the cross-workload Priority cleanup control is documented.

claims.where: Scope: Roles; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Approvers must be individual users.
claims.quote: Approvers must be individual users.

claims.claim: Mail-enabled security groups are not currently supported as approvers.
claims.quote: Mail-enabled security groups aren't currently supported.

claims.claim: The documented eDiscovery approver roles include Search And Purge, Hold, Review and Disposition Management.
claims.quote: eDiscovery admins | - Search And Purge- Hold- Review- Data Classification Content Viewer- Data Classification List Viewer- Disposition Management

claims.where: controls[3].note; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Auditing must be enabled at least one day before creating and running the first policy.
claims.quote: Enable auditing at least one day before you create and run the first Priority Cleanup policy.

claims.claim: Priority Cleanup Viewer allows visibility of policies and settings but not changes or policy creation.
claims.quote: the Priority Cleanup Viewer role allows only the visibility of priority cleanup policies and settings without the ability to make changes or create new policies.

claims.claim: Required approver roles must be assigned before policy creation.
claims.quote: Assign the required roles to each approver before policy creation.

claims.claim: The permanent deletion option is reached through the stated Purview Solutions, Data Lifecycle Management, Priority cleanup and creation path.
claims.quote: go to Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup. Select + Create a priority cleanup. ... On the Choose what to do with the content page, select Delete data permanently.

claims.claim: A PowerShell or API call documented to create a permanent-deletion Priority Cleanup policy was not found.
claims.quote: Searched: "Priority cleanup" "permanent" "PowerShell". Read New-ComplianceTag and feature setup; search returned retention-policy/rule PriorityCleanup switches but no documented permanent-deletion selection or complete creation call.

claims.claim: The tenant control is under Purview Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup settings > Configuration.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management. From the top right, select Priority cleanup settings. From the Configuration page, turn off the control for priority cleanup, and select Save.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or API equivalent for the tenant Priority Cleanup switch is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Priority cleanup" "tenant" "PowerShell" disable; Priority cleanup permanent deletion PowerShell API approval tenant settings disable permanent deletion billing licensing. Read the tenant-switch instructions; results document UI, not an automation equivalent.

claims.claim: Permanent-deletion approvals are reached through Purview Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > Pending cleanups.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, go to Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > Pending cleanups.

claims.claim: No documented PowerShell or API equivalent for approving these items was found.
claims.quote: Searched: "Priority cleanup" "approv" "API"; "priority cleanup" "approve" "powershell". Read feature approval instructions and returned Security & Compliance PowerShell retention-policy/rule references; none documents an approval call.

claims.claim: Each approver sees only items assigned to them for approval.
claims.quote: each person that accesses the Priority cleanup > Pending cleanups page sees only items that they're assigned to approve.

claims.claim: Policy details and the cleanup ID are reached through Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > policy details.
claims.quote: Go to Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup and open the policy details. Copy the cleanup ID.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog supports the printed StartDate, EndDate, Operations and FreeText filters for the audit search.
claims.quote: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -EndDate <ExDateTime> -StartDate <ExDateTime> ... [-FreeText <String>] ... [-Operations <String[]>] ... The FreeText parameter filters the log entries by the specified text string. ... The Operations parameter filters the log entries by operation.

claims.where: controls[3].api; controls[3].note; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: PriorityCleanupFileDeleted is the audit operation indicating permanent deletion by Priority Cleanup.
claims.quote: Check for the PriorityCleanupFileDeleted operation, which indicates that Priority Cleanup permanently deleted an item.

claims.claim: The cleanup ID is used as the keyword search string in auditing.
claims.quote: Copy the cleanup ID. In the auditing solution, use the cleanup ID as the keyword search string.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The tenant switch blocks creation of new Priority Cleanup policies for Exchange as well as SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: When you turn off priority cleanup, you're turning it off for Exchange as well as for SharePoint and OneDrive. ... New priority cleanup policies can't be created until you turn on the control and select Save again.

claims.claim: Security & Compliance PowerShell's New-ComplianceTag reference lists a PriorityCleanup parameter and parameter set without describing permanent-deletion policy creation.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell. ... ### PriorityCleanup ... [-PriorityCleanup] ... ### -PriorityCleanup ... {{ Fill PriorityCleanup Description }}

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, with rights available through eligible suites or add-on plans rather than a documented deletion meter.
claims.quote: To use the Priority cleanup policy to apply labels that bypass existing retention or eDiscovery holds, the following licenses provide user rights: ... Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 ... Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW ... Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection and Governance

claims.claim: MC1261587 asks organisations to update internal governance or compliance documentation.
claims.quote: Update internal governance or compliance documentation to reflect this new deletion capability.

claims.claim: Set-RetentionCompliancePolicy has a PriorityCleanup parameter.
claims.quote: ### -PriorityCleanup ... Type: SwitchParameter ... Parameter sets (All)
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/set-retentioncompliancepolicy to sources for this parameter mention.

claims.claim: New-RetentionComplianceRule has a PriorityCleanup parameter.
claims.quote: ### -PriorityCleanup ... Type: SwitchParameter ... Parameter sets (All)
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/new-retentioncompliancerule to sources for this parameter mention.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks administrators to check or set has a corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Check who holds the Priority Cleanup Admin role' and 'Enable auditing at least one day before the first policy is created.' Table: policy creation, tenant switch, approvals and monitoring; no role-assignment or auditing-enablement row.
claims.fix: The Before rollout instructions to review/remove role assignments, assign approver roles and enable auditing have no corresponding control rows. Remove those checklist instructions; retain the documented role and auditing prerequisites elsewhere rather than adding unverified control paths.

claims.claim: A single Priority Cleanup policy cannot cover Exchange, SharePoint and OneDrive together.
claims.quote: As a result of these differences, you can't create a cleanup policy for all three locations in same policy.
